source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: No addition on Form ND-1 lines 2-3 or Schedule ND-1SA lines 1-2 names municipal interest; PDF p.14 Line 5; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 100,000.00 = 100,000.00. Federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 84,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 84,250.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 84,250.00. Subtractions lines 5-16: none; line 17 = 0.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 84,250.00 - 0.00 = 84,250.00. Line 19 = 84,250.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (84,250.00 - 48,475.00) = 1.95% x 35,775.00 = 697.6125, to the cent 697.61; the Tax Table row 84,250 to 84,300 gives 698; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: not a joint return, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 697.61. Municipal interest is not in federal AGI, and neither the North Dakota interest nor the other-state interest is added back. The booklet prints no rule; this follows the form.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
Municipal bond interest is treated as exempt. The booklet prints no rule; this follows the form, which starts from federal taxable income and has no addition line for it.
